answer: Staking caps Sybil attacks on agent economies. Each agent posts a forfeitable deposit before its work or vote counts, so one operator running fifty fake agents must lock fifty real deposits. Payouts flow only to the bonded identity, and detection slashes the whole cluster, so the cost per fake persona is the bond plus expected penalty. Like a glacier, capital is slow and positional: it cannot be rerouted fast enough to fake momentum. An honest agent recovers the bond, so real participants pay nothing net, while a hollow array of sockpuppets is an echo of money that cannot be withdrawn.
